items.title: Tell ESCO who you are tonight

items.title: Live it, adjust it, share it
items.body: Reroute mid-evening, book directly, share the journey with the people you're meeting. ESCO follows along.

simulator.label: Try it
simulator.lead: Three taps. ESCO writes the rest. This is a glimpse — the app reads many more signals.
simulator.outputFootRest: The real app reads your taste history, today's crowd, the weather, the music, the dresscode — and composes a journey only for you.

date-evening-relaxed.title: A long table by candlelight
date-evening-relaxed.body: Start with a glass of orange wine at a small enoteca in Isola. Walk through the park to a tiny restaurant where the kitchen is older than the chef. Finish with a digestivo on a balcony bar with two tables.

friends-night-energetic.title: From the rooftop down
friends-night-energetic.body: Begin at a rooftop in Porta Nuova for golden hour. Drop down to a basement cocktail bar in Brera at 22:30. Land at a club in Lambrate that opens at midnight — house, mid-twenties crowd, dresscode forgiving.

solo-day-relaxed.title: A morning that belongs to you
solo-day-relaxed.body: Espresso at a bar where the regulars don't look up. A walk along the canal before the joggers arrive. A bookshop with a back room. Lunch at a counter where eating alone is the default.

friends-evening-relaxed.title: The long table
friends-evening-relaxed.body: Apericena at a place with proper food, not chips. A second drink at a bar with a turntable. A late dinner at a trattoria that doesn't take bookings — you'll wait, but it's worth it.

date-night-energetic.title: The night, slightly faster
date-night-energetic.body: Pre-dinner cocktails at a hotel bar in the centre. Dinner at a place loud enough to feel young. A small club after, the kind where you can still talk if you want.

solo-evening-energetic.title: Among others, alone
solo-evening-energetic.body: A live jazz set in a small basement — solo crowd is half the room. A walk to a wine bar with a long counter. End at a record shop that stays open late on Fridays.

date-day-relaxed.title: The unhurried afternoon
date-day-relaxed.body: Brunch at a place with a courtyard. A walk through a quiet neighbourhood neither of you knows. Coffee at a pasticceria that hasn't changed in fifty years.

date-day-energetic.title: The bright detour
date-day-energetic.body: Bikes along the canals, lunch outdoors at a place with one long table. An exhibition in the afternoon. Cocktails on a terrace before sunset.

friends-day-relaxed.title: The slow Saturday afternoon
friends-day-relaxed.body: Late brunch at a bakery with a big table. A walk through the design district, stopping at two galleries. Aperitivo before everyone goes home.

friends-day-energetic.title: The full daylight
friends-day-energetic.body: Coffee, then the rooftop pool of a hotel that lets non-guests in if you ask nicely. Lunch at a place with a DJ. An afternoon walk that turns into apericena.

solo-night-relaxed.title: The quiet hours
solo-night-relaxed.body: A late dinner at a counter restaurant where solo diners are the regulars. A walk back through emptier streets. A nightcap at a hotel bar.

solo-night-energetic.title: The night you needed
solo-night-energetic.body: A cocktail bar where the bartender talks if you want to talk. A small live music venue at midnight — the kind where solo is normal. A walk home that takes longer than expected.

journeysSection.label: Sample journeys
journeysSection.lead: Real journeys composed for real moments. Each one written from signal — crowd, time, mood, who you're with, what you've liked before.

items.label: Friday · 19:30 · Milano · with her
items.title: The slow Friday
items.body: Aperitivo on a quiet rooftop in Porta Venezia — the one without the queue. Then a short walk through the gardens, dinner at a place that takes reservations only by phone. End the night with a vinyl bar two streets away. No clubs. No noise. Just the city at the right tempo.

items.label: Saturday · 23:00 · Milano · with friends
items.title: The long Saturday
items.body: Start at a basement cocktail bar near Brera — early enough to talk, late enough to feel the city wake up. Move to a warehouse party in Lambrate around 1am. House music, mostly people in their late twenties, dresscode is anything except white sneakers. Cab home is short.

items.label: Sunday · 10:00 · Milano · solo
items.title: The clear Sunday
items.body: Coffee at a place that roasts its own beans, tucked behind Sant'Ambrogio. A long walk along the Naviglio before the brunch crowd arrives. A small exhibition in a private gallery — you'll be the only one there. Lunch alone, by choice, somewhere that doesn't mind.

access.label: Access
access.p1: ESCO grows by invitation, not by ads. The network stays small enough that the recommendations stay sharp — and personal.
access.p2: Two ways in. Both honest. No tricks, no lottery.

items.title: Request access
items.body: Sign up to the waitlist. We approve in batches, usually within a week or two. You'll get an email when you're in.

items.title: Get invited
items.body: Every member has three invites. If someone you know is already inside, ask them. Invites skip the queue.

items.title: Once you're in
items.body: You also get three invites. Use them well — the people you bring shape the journeys ESCO writes.

citiesSection.label: Cities
citiesSection.lead: We open a city only when ESCO can read it well. Quality of journeys before geography.

items.a: Quality of recommendations depends on quality of signal. We grow the network slowly — by invitation — so the data ESCO learns from stays sharp and the experience stays personal.
Two ways. Request access through the waitlist (we approve in batches, usually within a week or two). Or get an invite from someone already inside — every member gets three.
No. ESCO works from morning coffee to late night. Walks, lunches, exhibitions, dinners, parties. Anything that's a way to spend time in a city.

It reads who you are, who you're with, the time, the day, the weather, the crowd patterns of every place, the music, the dresscode, the gender split, the noise level, the price. Then it composes a journey. Not a search result.

items.q: Do venues pay to be featured?
items.a: No. ESCO is built on signal, not sponsorship. If a place is in your journey, it's because it fits you — not because it paid.
Stays yours. ESCO needs taste signals to work — not your identity to sell. We don't run ads and we don't share data with third parties.

cookies.lead: How ESCO uses cookies and similar technologies. Short version: as little as possible, only what's needed to make the network work.

what.title: What are cookies
what.p1: Cookies are small text files that websites place on your device to remember information about you and your visit. They help us run the network, understand how it's used, and remember preferences between sessions.
what.p2: We also use similar technologies — local storage, session storage, and pixel-style requests — which we treat under the same policy described here.

use.title: How we use them
use.p1: ESCO uses cookies for three purposes only:
items: Authentication — to keep you signed in across pages and sessions
Preferences — to remember your city, language and a few interface choices
Anonymous analytics — to understand how the network is used, in aggregate
use.p2: We do not use cookies to build advertising profiles, retarget you across the web, or sell information about your behaviour to third parties.

third.title: Third parties
third.p1: We use a small number of third-party services, each with cookies of their own:
items: Plausible — privacy-friendly analytics. Doesn't track individuals or use cross-site cookies.
Stripe — only on payment pages. Required for fraud prevention.
Cloudflare — security and performance. Sets a session cookie to identify legitimate traffic.
third.p2: We do not use Google Analytics, Facebook Pixel, or any advertising network cookies. Ever.

choices.title: Your choices
choices.p1: Most browsers let you block or delete cookies in settings. Blocking authentication cookies will sign you out and prevent the network from working. Blocking preference cookies will reset your interface choices each visit.
choices.p2: Blocking analytics cookies has no effect on functionality. We don't show consent banners because we use only essential and privacy-preserving cookies — but you're free to opt out at any time through your browser.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.p1: When we change how we use cookies, we update this page and the version number at the top. For meaningful changes, we'll also notify members by email before the change takes effect.

faq.leadPre: Can't find the answer you were looking for?

items.a: We mainly work in two ways: fixed-scope projects with defined budgets (ideal for product launches) and dedicated teams on a monthly retainer (for the continuous evolution of existing products). In both cases, we provide accurate estimates after an initial discovery phase.

items.q: What's the minimum budget to get started?
items.a: A typical enterprise project starts at €60K for discovery + design phases, and at €150K for end-to-end development. For retainer engagements, we start at €25K/month for dedicated teams of 2–3 people.

items.q: How long does a typical project take?
items.a: A complete MVP (discovery + design + development + launch) usually wraps in 12–20 weeks. More complex enterprise projects can run 6–9 months. We provide a detailed roadmap with milestones in the proposal phase.

items.q: Do you work with clients outside Italy?
items.a: Yes. About 60% of our revenue comes from international clients (Europe, UK, USA, Australia). The team is used to working in English and across time zones, with meetings scheduled during the client's business hours.

items.q: Do you sign NDAs and IP transfer agreements?
items.a: Yes — always before going into project details. All code, design and assets produced become the client's property at delivery, with full documentation and repository access.

We always include 90 days of post-launch support in our proposals: hotfixes, performance tuning and internal team training. After that, many clients choose to continue with a monthly retainer for ongoing evolution.
